questions.text:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A : If we move from poles to equator, the direction of acceleration due to gravity of earth always points towards the center of earth without any variation in its magnitude.
Reason R : At equator, the direction of acceleration due to the gravity is towards the center of earth.
In the light of above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D:
A is false but R is true

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)

Sol.

Effective acceleration due to gravity is the resultant of $\mathrm{g} \& \mathrm{rw}^{2}$ whose direction \& magnitude depends upon $\theta$. Hence assertion is false.

When $\theta=0^{\circ}$ (at equator), effective acceleration is radially inward.

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor with plate area A and plate separation $\mathrm{d}=2 \mathrm{~m}$ has a capacitance of $4 \mu \mathrm{~F}$. The new capacitance of the system if half of the space between them is filled with a dielectric material of dielectric constant $\mathrm{K}=3$ (as shown in figure) will be :

options.D:
$8 \mu \mathrm{~F}$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)

Sol. $\mathrm{C}_{\text {original }}=\frac{\mathrm{A} \varepsilon_{0}}{\mathrm{~d}}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{C}_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{A} \varepsilon_{0}}{\mathrm{~d} / 2}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~A} \varepsilon_{0}}{\mathrm{~d}}=\mathrm{C} \\
\mathrm{C}_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{KA} \varepsilon_{0}}{\mathrm{~d} / 2}=\frac{2 \mathrm{KA} \varepsilon_{0}}{\mathrm{~d}}=\frac{6 \mathrm{~A} \varepsilon_{0}}{\mathrm{~d}}=3 \mathrm{C}
\end{array}$$
$\mathrm{C}_{1} \& \mathrm{C}_{2}$ are in series
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{C}_{\text {new }} & =\frac{\mathrm{C}_{1} \mathrm{C}_{2}}{\mathrm{C}_{1}+\mathrm{C}_{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{C} \times 3 \mathrm{C}}{\mathrm{C}+3 \mathrm{C}}=\frac{3 \mathrm{C}}{4} \\
& =\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{2 \mathrm{~A} \varepsilon_{0}}{\mathrm{~d}}=\frac{3}{2} \times \frac{\mathrm{A} \varepsilon_{0}}{\mathrm{~d}} \\
\mathrm{C}_{\text {new }} & =\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{C}_{\text {original }} \\
& =\frac{3}{2} \times 4=6 \mu \mathrm{~F}
\end{aligned}$$

questions.text: Sixty four conducting drops each of radius 0.02 m and each carrying a charge of $5 \mu \mathrm{C}$ are combined to form a bigger drop. The ratio of surface density of bigger drop to the smaller drop will be :

options.D:
$8: 1$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. Let $\mathrm{R}=$ radius of combined drop
r = radius of smaller drop
Volume will remain same
$$\begin{array}{l}
\quad \frac{4}{3} \pi R^{3}=64 \times \frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3} \\
\quad R=4 r \\
Q=64 q ;
\end{array}$$
q : charge of smaller drop
Q : Charge of combined drop
$$\begin{array}{l}

=64 \frac{r^{2}}{16 r^{2}}=4 \\
\frac{\sigma_{\text {bigger }}}{\sigma_{\text {smaller }}}=\frac{4}{1}
\end{array}$$

questions.text:
A radioactive nucleus can decay by two different processes. Half-life for the first process is 3.0 hours while it is 4.5 hours for the second process.
The effective half- life of the nucleus will be :

options.D:
1.80 hours

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. $\lambda_{\text {eq }}=\lambda_{1}+\lambda_{2}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\frac{\ln 2}{\left(t_{1 / 2}\right)_{\mathrm{eq}}}=\frac{\ln 2}{\left(t_{1 / 2}\right)_{1}}+\frac{\ln 2}{\left(t_{1 / 2}\right)_{2}} \\
\left(t_{1 / 2}\right)_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{\left(t_{1 / 2}\right)_{1} \times\left(t_{1 / 2}\right)_{2}}{\left(t_{1 / 2}\right)_{1}+\left(t_{1 / 2}\right)_{2}} \\
=\frac{3 \times 4.5}{3+4.5}=\frac{3 \times 4.5}{7.5}=\frac{3 \times 3}{5}=1.8 \mathrm{hr}
\end{array}$$

questions.text: A sinusoidal wave $\mathrm{y}(\mathrm{t})=40 \sin \left(10 \times 10^{6} \pi \mathrm{t}\right)$ is amplitude modulated by another sinusoidal wave $\mathrm{x}(\mathrm{t})=20 \sin (1000 \pi \mathrm{t})$. The amplitude of minimum frequency component of modulated signal is :

options.D:
10

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. $\quad y(t)=40 \sin \left(10 \times 10^{6} \pi t\right)$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{x}(\mathrm{t})=20 \sin (1000 \pi \mathrm{t}) \\
\Rightarrow \omega_{\mathrm{c}}=10^{7} \pi \\
\omega_{\mathrm{m}}=10^{3} \pi \\
\mathrm{~A}_{\mathrm{C}}=40 \\
\mathrm{~A}_{\mathrm{m}}=20
\end{array}$$

Equation of modulated wave $=\left(\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{C}}+\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{m}} \sin \omega_{\mathrm{m}} \mathrm{t}\right) \sin \omega_{\mathrm{c}} \mathrm{t}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
=A_{c}\left(1+\frac{A_{m}}{A_{c}} \sin \omega_{m} t\right) \sin \omega_{c} t \\
=A_{c}\left(1+\mu \sin \omega_{m} t\right) \sin \omega_{c} t, \quad \mu=\frac{A_{m}}{A_{c}}
\end{array}$$
$$=A_{c} \sin \omega_{c} t+\frac{\mu A_{c}}{2}\left[\cos \left(\omega_{c}-\omega_{m}\right) t-\cos \left(\omega_{c}+\omega_{m}\right) t\right]$$

Amplitude of minimum frequency = $\frac{\mu \mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{c}}}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{m}}}{\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{c}}} \times \frac{\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{c}}}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{m}}}{2}=10$
